title: Green Ash: Ancient Green Ashes You Can Visit
meta_description: Delaware's champion green ash, 42.7 metres tall, outlived the beetle that killed most of the state's ash. Two more in the Bronx and Barcelona.
intro: The emerald ash borer, a beetle from Asia, has killed most of Delaware's ash trees since the 2010s, and the state's champion green ash was still standing when the Delaware Forest Service ranked it in October 2024. It grows at Hagley, the museum estate outside Wilmington, 42.7 metres tall on a trunk 4.22 metres round. In the Bronx, NYC Parks treats the green ash behind the Crotona Park playground against the same beetle at regular intervals, and its forestry inventory rated the tree in good condition in September 2026. The species comes from the flooded river bottoms of eastern North America and can stand with its roots underwater for weeks at a time, which makes the third one a long way from home. Barcelona planted it in 1924 in the Sot de l'Estany, the damp old quarry pit at the bottom of the Montjuic botanical garden, where it has reached 32 metres. The pit has been closed to visitors since the landslides of July 2026. Nobody has published an age for the two American trees.
